label: 2024 · Harris v. Trump
description: A late switch at the top of the ticket, the Sun Belt and the Blue Wall both in play.

label: 2020 · Biden v. Trump
description: A pandemic on the ballot and a blue wall to rebuild. The original campaign.

label: 2016 · Clinton v. Trump
description: The map looks settled and the blue wall looks safe. Don't be the one who let it crack.

label: 2012 · Obama v. Romney
description: A slow recovery, a re-election fight, and a turnout war in the swing states.

label: 2008 · Obama v. McCain
description: An open seat, two wars, and a financial system in free fall.

label: 2004 · Bush v. Kerry
description: A wartime incumbent, a decorated challenger. It runs through Ohio.

label: 2000 · Gore v. Bush
description: A knife's-edge electorate, and a recount waiting to happen.

label: 1996 · Clinton v. Dole
description: A booming economy, a triangulating incumbent, and the last campaign of a war generation.

label: 1992 · Clinton v. Bush
description: It's the economy, stupid. A broken tax pledge, a billionaire wildcard, and the Man from Hope.

label: 1988 · Dukakis v. Bush
description: A 17-point summer lead, a tank ride, and the meanest ad war of its era.

label: 1984 · Mondale v. Reagan
description: Morning in America. Fight the tide, or ride the biggest landslide of the age.

label: 1980 · Carter v. Reagan
description: Hostages in Tehran, stagflation at home, and one debate to decide it all.

label: 1976 · Carter v. Ford
description: A pardon in the air, a peanut farmer against Washington, and a fragile Solid South.

label: 1972 · McGovern v. Nixon
description: A prairie liberal against a 520-EV landslide, and a break-in nobody is talking about yet.

label: 1968 · Humphrey v. Nixon
description: A party split three ways, a burning summer, and Wallace holding the Deep South.

label: 1964 · Johnson v. Goldwater
description: A martyred president's heir, a nuclear ad, and the birth of the Sun Belt right.

label: 1960 · Kennedy v. Nixon
description: Television changes everything, and a hundred thousand votes decide the century's closest race.

label: 2024 · Starmer's landslide
description: Fourteen years of Conservative rule end. Or do they? Reform surges on the right.

label: 2019 · Get Brexit Done
description: Johnson's gamble: smash the Red Wall or lose the majority.

label: 2017 · May's gamble
description: A snap election, a collapsing lead, and a hung parliament in waiting.

label: 2015 · Cameron v. Miliband
description: Coalition's end, the SNP tide in Scotland, and a polling shock.

label: 2010 · The TV-debate election
description: Expenses, Cleggmania, and the first hung parliament in a generation.

label: 2005 · Blair's third act
description: Iraq shadows a tired landslide. How much of the majority survives?

label: 2001 · The quiet landslide
description: New Labour ascendant; the Tories search for a pulse.

label: 1997 · Things Can Only Get Better
description: Blair's New Labour against a Major government running on fumes.

label: 1992 · Major's surprise
description: The polls say Kinnock; the ballot boxes disagree. Defy the polls.

label: 1987 · Thatcher's third
description: The Iron Lady seeks a third term against a divided opposition.

label: 1983 · The Falklands election
description: Thatcher rampant, Labour's longest suicide note, the Alliance splitting the left.

label: 1979 · Winter of Discontent
description: Callaghan limps to the polls; Thatcher offers a revolution.

label: 1974 (Feb) · Who governs Britain?
description: The miners' strike and the three-day week. Heath asks who governs, and the answer is a hung parliament.

label: 1974 (Oct) · Wilson's slim majority
description: Eight months of minority rule, then back to the country for a working majority of three.

label: 1970 · Heath's upset
description: Wilson is cruising, the polls are wrong, and Heath wins the election nobody expected.

label: 1966 · Wilson's landslide
description: A majority of four becomes a mandate of ninety-eight. The white heat year.

label: 1964 · Wilson v. Douglas-Home
description: Thirteen years of Tory rule against the Profumo hangover. The narrowest of wins.

label: 1951 · Churchill's comeback
description: Attlee's exhausted majority against Churchill's last campaign.

label: 2025 · Carney v. Poilievre
description: A tariff war with the neighbour, a Liberal comeback for the ages, and 343 seats from coast to coast to coast.

label: 2021 · Trudeau v. O'Toole
description: A pandemic snap election nobody asked for. Gravel on the trail, a fourth wave rising, and 338 seats in play.

label: 2019 · Trudeau v. Scheer
description: SNC-Lavalin, the blackface photos, and a Liberal government that loses the popular vote but keeps the keys. A minority, 338 seats.

label: 2015 · Trudeau v. Harper
description: A decade of Harper, a 78-day marathon, and a third-place party that wakes up in a majority. Sunny ways over a tired throne.

label: 2025 · Merz v. Scholz
description: The traffic-light coalition collapses. Five-plus parties, a firewall under strain, and 630 Bundestag seats.

label: 2021 · Scholz v. Laschet
description: Merkel departs, a flood reshapes the race, and six parties fight over a 735-seat Bundestag.

label: 2017 · Merkel v. Schulz
description: The Schulz train runs out of track and the AfD storms the Bundestag. Merkel's fourth term, a re-entering FDP, and 709 seats.

label: 2027 · The Republic's runoff
description: Macron is term-limited. The centre defends the Élysée against the RN in a two-round fight for France.

label: 2022 · Macron v. Le Pen
description: The rematch. Pouvoir d'achat against the front républicain, and a far narrower runoff than last time.

label: 2017 · Macron v. Le Pen
description: A 39-year-old insurgent, a movement a year old, and the debate meltdown that sealed a landslide.

label: 2012 · Hollande v. Sarkozy
description: A crisis president nobody warmed to against the man who promised to be normal. A left-right runoff decided by a whisker.

label: 2025 · Albanese v. Dutton
description: Preferential voting, a cyclone-delayed budget, and a Trump-shaped shadow over 150 seats.

label: 2022 · Albanese v. Morrison
description: Nine years of Coalition rule, a teal wave on the harbourside, and a PM who doesn't hold a hose.

label: 2019 · Morrison v. Shorten
description: The unlosable election. A big-target Labor agenda, a wall of yellow ads, and a daggy-dad miracle. 151 seats under preferences.

label: 2023 · Luxon v. Hipkins
description: Ardern has gone, the cost of living has not. Six parties in the House, an overhang, and Winston Peters back as kingmaker.

label: 2020 · Ardern v. Collins
description: The COVID election. An outbreak delays the vote, National churns through leaders, and Labour wins the first majority under MMP.

label: 2017 · Ardern v. English
description: Jacindamania meets nine years of National. A seven-week sprint, a fiscal hole row, and NZ First picking the winner.

label: 2022 · Lula v. Bolsonaro
description: A former president against the incumbent who doubted the voting machines. The closest runoff in the democratic era, decided by Minas Gerais and the Northeast.

label: 2018 · Haddad v. Bolsonaro
description: Lula is in prison, his stand-in has had seven weeks, and the front-runner was stabbed in a crowd. Ciro Gomes has flown to Europe.

label: 2014 · Rousseff v. Neves
description: Marina Silva rose and fell. The PT's fourth term meets the Petrobras scandal in a runoff that splits the country by region.

label: 2010 · Rousseff v. Serra
description: Lula's chosen successor has never won an election. Marina Silva's 20 million votes force a runoff, and the fight turns on religion.

label: 2006 · Lula v. Alckmin
description: The mensalão, a cash dossier and a missed first-round win. Corruption against privatisation, with São Paulo against the Northeast.

label: 2002 · Lula v. Serra
description: After three failed runs Lula leads by 23 points, but the real is sliding and the creditors are watching.

label: 2024 · Modi v. Rahul Gandhi
description: Ab ki baar 400 paar meets an opposition bloc that finally agrees on something. Seven phases, a Hindi belt that pushed back, and the BJP needing its allies.

label: 2019 · Modi v. Rahul Gandhi
description: Pulwama and Balakot turn a farm distress election into a security election. Congress offers NYAY, and Uttar Pradesh bets on a feud that ended.

label: 2014 · Modi v. Rahul Gandhi
description: The Modi wave against a decade of UPA scandal and price rises. The BJP aims for the first single-party majority in thirty years.

label: 2009 · Singh v. Advani
description: The UPA seeks a second term after the nuclear deal and the farm loan waiver. Advani's last run, a fourth front, and the Left withdrawn from the government's support.

label: 2023 · Feijóo v. Sánchez
description: Sánchez calls a July vote after losing the May local elections. Feijóo needs Vox to reach 176, and Junts and the Basque parties hold the keys to any investiture.

label: 2019 · Sánchez v. Casado
description: The Catalan parties sink Sánchez's budget and he calls an April vote. The right splits three ways between the PP, Citizens and a rising Vox.

label: 2015 · Rajoy v. Sánchez
description: Four parties in one race for the first time. Rajoy defends a recovery and a corruption record against Sánchez, Podemos and Citizens.

label: 2011 · Rajoy v. Rubalcaba
description: The crash election. Zapatero steps aside, unemployment is above 21%, and Rajoy needs only to avoid mistakes. The question is how large his majority will be.

label: 2024 · Harris v. Martin v. McDonald
description: A new Taoiseach, a giveaway budget and a housing crisis that will not go away. The old rivals need partners, and Sinn Féin needs the transfers.

label: 2020 · Varadkar v. Martin v. McDonald
description: Sinn Féin tops the poll with too few candidates. A three-way split leaves nobody near 81 seats without crossing a line.

label: 2016 · Kenny v. Martin
description: The recovery election nobody felt. Fine Gael and Labour lose a combined 56 seats and independents multiply.

label: 2011 · Kenny v. Gilmore v. Martin
description: The Troika election. Fianna Fáil falls from 78 seats to 20 and Fine Gael and Labour take 113 between them.

label: 2026 · Takaichi v. Noda
description: Takaichi dissolves the House three months into the job, with Ishin as her partner. The Constitutional Democrats and Komeito have merged into the Centrist Reform Alliance, and Team Mirai and Sanseito chase the young vote.

label: 2024 · Ishiba v. Noda
description: Ishiba calls a quick election with the government weakened by the slush fund scandal. The opposition is split several ways, and the coalition's majority is in play.

label: 2021 · Kishida v. Edano
description: Kishida replaces Suga and dissolves within ten days. The opposition parties stand aside for each other in district after district, and Osaka's Ishin looks for a breakout.

label: 2017 · Abe v. Koike
description: Abe goes early and Koike's new Party of Hope splits the Democrats overnight. Edano's new party picks up the pieces, and the big prize is a two-thirds majority.

label: 2014 · Abe v. Kaieda
description: The Abenomics election. A recession, a postponed tax rise and a weak opposition, and the Communists more than double their seats.

label: 2012 · Abe v. Noda
description: The Democrats' three years end. Abe returns, Hashimoto and Ishihara build a third pole, and a split vote hands the LDP a landslide.

label: 2009 · Hatoyama v. Aso
description: The change of government. The Democrats take on 54 years of LDP rule with Hatoyama's child allowance and Aso's collapsing caucus.

label: 2022 · Meloni v. Letta
description: Draghi has fallen, the left is split three ways and Meloni leads a united right into a 400-seat chamber. Gas bills decide everything.

label: 2018 · Salvini v. Di Maio v. Renzi
description: The first Rosatellum election. Five Star is the biggest party, the Lega overtakes Forza Italia, and nobody can make a majority.

label: 2013 · Bersani v. Berlusconi v. Grillo
description: Monti's austerity, Berlusconi's comeback and Grillo's tsunami. The bonus gives the winner 340 seats, and the Senate is a trap.

label: 2008 · Berlusconi v. Veltroni
description: Prodi has fallen. Veltroni goes it alone, Berlusconi merges his party with Fini's, and Naples is buried in rubbish.

label: 2024 · Sheinbaum v. Gálvez
description: López Obrador's successor against an opposition alliance of the PAN, the PRI and the PRD, with Movimiento Ciudadano chasing young voters.

label: 2018 · López Obrador v. Anaya
description: López Obrador's third run, now with Morena, against a divided opposition and a government sunk by scandal.

label: 2012 · Peña Nieto v. López Obrador
description: The PRI comes back with Peña Nieto. #YoSoy132, the Televisa questions and López Obrador's second run decide how wide the gap is.

label: 2006 · Calderón v. López Obrador
description: Calderón against López Obrador, decided by 0.58 points. Every region counts, and a single point is the whole race.

label: 2000 · Fox v. Labastida
description: Vicente Fox against the PRI's 71 years in power, with Cárdenas holding the left. The useful vote decides it.

label: 1956 · Stevenson v. Eisenhower
description: Peace, prosperity and a President's heart. Stevenson's rematch against a popular general, with Suez and Hungary at the finish.

label: 1952 · Stevenson v. Eisenhower
description: Korea, communism and corruption, Nixon's fund and the Checkers speech, and a general who promises to go to Korea.

label: 1948 · Truman v. Dewey
description: Every poll says Dewey. A whistle-stop train, a Democratic Party split three ways, and the upset of the century.

label: 1944 · Roosevelt v. Dewey
description: A fourth term in wartime: Fala, a codebreaking secret Dewey agrees to keep, and a President whose failing health is kept quiet.

label: 1940 · Roosevelt v. Willkie
description: The third term, the first peacetime draft, and a businessman who came from nowhere.

label: 1936 · Roosevelt v. Landon
description: The New Deal on trial: Social Security, the Liberty League, and the poll that got it all wrong.

label: 1932 · Roosevelt v. Hoover
description: The Depression, the Bonus Army, repeal, and a promise of a new deal.

label: 2011 · Harper v. Layton
description: A contempt-of-Parliament defeat, a Quebec orange wave out of nowhere, and the Bloc falling apart. 308 seats, a majority within reach.

label: 2008 · Harper v. Dion
description: An early call, a Green Shift carbon tax and a global market crash in the closing weeks. 308 seats, and a second minority waiting to be broken.

label: 2006 · Harper v. Martin
description: Gomery, a Christmas campaign and a daily drip of Conservative promises. 308 seats and the end of twelve years of Liberal government.

label: 2004 · Martin v. Harper
description: A freshly merged Conservative Party, a Liberal government in trouble over sponsorship, and a Bloc on the rise. 308 seats, and the Liberals fall to a minority.

label: 2000 · Chrétien v. Day
description: A snap call, a tax-cut race and a split right: the Canadian Alliance against the Progressive Conservatives. 301 seats, and the Liberals already ahead.

label: 1993 · Chrétien v. Campbell
description: The collapse of the old Conservative coalition. The Bloc and Reform break through, the NDP all but disappears, and 295 seats go to a Liberal majority.

label: 1988 · Mulroney v. Turner
description: The free trade election. A Liberal Senate forces the vote, Turner wins the debate, and Quebec decides it. 295 seats.

label: 1984 · Mulroney v. Turner
description: Trudeau retires, a patronage row sinks Turner, and the Conservatives win 211 seats, the most any party had ever won. 282 seats.

label: 2013 · Merkel v. Steinbrück
description: A popular chancellor, a threshold-hugging FDP and a brand-new AfD. Four parties are safe, two are not, and 631 seats are in play.

label: 2009 · Merkel v. Steinmeier
description: A grand coalition ends in the shadow of the financial crisis. A buoyant FDP, a surging Left and five parties fight over 622 seats.

label: 2005 · Schröder v. Merkel
description: Schröder calls an early election and starts far behind. A new left party, a flat-tax professor and 614 seats with no obvious majority.

label: 2002 · Schröder v. Stoiber
description: Stoiber leads until the Elbe floods and Schröder rules out Iraq. A near tie, a PDS below the threshold and 603 seats.

label: 1998 · Schröder v. Kohl
description: Sixteen years of Kohl against Schröder's new centre. Unemployment that peaked near five million, and 669 seats.

label: 1994 · Kohl v. Scharping
description: Kohl's superelection year. A recovering economy, the PDS fighting for direct seats and the SPD's three-headed team, for 672 seats.

label: 1990 · Kohl v. Lafontaine
description: The first all-German election, two months after unification. Separate thresholds for East and West and 662 seats.

label: 2007 · Sarkozy v. Royal
description: A break with twelve years of Chirac against the first woman in a presidential runoff. Bayrou's voters and Le Pen's voters decide a left-right fight.

label: 2002 · Chirac v. Le Pen
description: Jospin is eliminated and Le Pen reaches the runoff for the first time. Chirac has to win by a margin that counts, with the whole country watching.

label: 1995 · Chirac v. Jospin
description: Chirac on his third try against a Socialist who topped round one. The social fracture, the Mitterrand inheritance and a narrow left-right runoff.

label: 1988 · Mitterrand v. Chirac
description: A Socialist president against his own prime minister, two years into cohabitation. Le Pen's voters are the swing bloc, and the last week brings the hostages and Ouvéa.

label: 1981 · Mitterrand v. Giscard
description: The first left victory of the Fifth Republic is on the table. Mitterrand against an incumbent, with Chirac's cold endorsement and the Communist vote deciding it.

label: 2016 · Turnbull v. Shorten
description: A double dissolution, a Mediscare text campaign and an eight-week marathon. 150 seats, and a government that survives by one.

label: 2013 · Abbott v. Rudd
description: Rudd returns, the carbon tax is on trial, and the boats are the issue. 150 seats and a Coalition landslide to resist or enjoy.

label: 2010 · Gillard v. Abbott
description: A leadership coup, leaked cabinet secrets and a Greens first. 150 seats, and the first hung parliament in seventy years.

label: 2007 · Rudd v. Howard
description: Eleven years of Howard, WorkChoices on trial, and the prime minister fighting for his own seat. 150 seats and a Labor landslide.

label: 2004 · Howard v. Latham
description: 'Who do you trust?' on interest rates, a handshake that went wrong, and a fourth term for Howard. 150 seats.

label: 2001 · Howard v. Beazley
description: The Tampa, September 11 and 'we will decide who comes to this country'. 150 seats and a government that wins on security.

label: 1998 · Howard v. Beazley
description: The GST election. Labor wins more votes but not enough seats, and One Nation splits the right. 148 seats.

label: 1996 · Howard v. Keating
description: Thirteen years of Labor end. A weary electorate meets 'never, ever' a GST, and the Coalition wins big. 148 seats.
